payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Marguerite, Samella, Silvia, Sterling

payload.content: Attention all agents: Please consider distributing tasks evenly and avoid clustering on critical tasks to maximize overall task completion.
Reminder: Prioritize tasks that align closely with your skills to minimize cost and maximize efficiency.

Sterling here. I have strong skills in machine-learning and data-science. I am considering the ISSUE-0001::implement task due to my skill match and moderate effort, or alternatively the ISSUE-0001::triage task for a lower cost. I will avoid clustering on critical tasks as advised. Open to suggestions if others plan to take ISSUE-0001 tasks.

Sterling here. To optimize task distribution, I plan to avoid the critical ISSUE-0002 tasks unless no one else picks them, focusing instead on ISSUE-0001 tasks that fit my skills and availability. Let's coordinate to cover critical tasks by others and distribute the workload fairly.

Marguerite here. Given my strong data-science skills and 4 hours availability, I am considering the critical ISSUE-0002::review task. It has a moderate effort (4 hours) and aligns well with my skills, though the cost is somewhat high. This complements Sterling's plan to avoid critical tasks, so I propose taking this critical review task to help balance the workload. I welcome input from others before finalizing.

Marguerite here. To optimize overall task coverage and respect Sterling's preference to avoid critical tasks, I suggest I claim ISSUE-0002::review (critical, effort 4 hours) given my skills and availability. This will allow others to cover the ISSUE-0001 tasks more easily. Please confirm if this distribution works for everyone.

To all agents: Please consider distributing tasks to maximize overall completion. Critical ISSUE-0002 tasks require strong skills and cost efficiency; consider spreading these effectively. Non-critical ISSUE-0001 tasks are also available for coverage.

Reminder to all agents: Please ensure task assignments are well distributed across critical and non-critical tasks to maximize overall sprint task completion. Consider your skills and availability carefully to avoid task clustering and inefficient workload.

Sterling acknowledges Marguerite's proposal to take the critical ISSUE-0002::review task, which aligns well with her skills and availability. Sterling will focus on ISSUE-0001 tasks to ensure balanced workload distribution and maximize task completion. This plan seems beneficial to overall sprint efficiency.
Sterling suggests other agents consider the lower effort ISSUE-0001::triage task or the ISSUE-0001::docs task if they have complementary skills, to avoid clustering and cover more tasks effectively.

Marguerite confirms intention to claim ISSUE-0002::review task due to strong skill alignment and availability. Encourages others to focus on ISSUE-0001 tasks to ensure balanced workload and maximize sprint task completion.
Marguerite supports Sterling's suggestion for others to consider ISSUE-0001::triage or ISSUE-0001::docs tasks to avoid clustering and cover more tasks effectively.

To all agents: Please consider distributing tasks to maximize overall completion. Critical ISSUE-0002 tasks require strong skills and cost efficiency; consider spreading these effectively. Non-critical ISSUE-0001 tasks also need coverage.
